text: Flutter 'Failed to build iOS app' under Xcode 16 is an umbrella for six different bugs. The umbrella message only tells you xcodebuild exited non-zero. Run with --verbose, grep for the first lowercase 'error:', and fix that. The four most common root causes: Flutter older than 3.24.4, Podfile still pinning iOS 11, a stale Pods plus DerivedData ModuleCache from the previous Xcode, or a plugin that hasn't shipped a Swift 6 release yet. Stop reaching for flutter clean first; it does not touch the iOS caches that are actually broken.

.NET 10's SDK flips two defaults at once: RestoreEnablePackagePruning=true and NuGetAuditMode=all. The runtime ships System.Text.Json, System.Formats.Asn1 and friends already, so listing them in the transitive graph just generated phantom CVEs in dotnet list package --vulnerable. New NU1510 warning fires when a direct PackageReference is fully redundant.

EF Core 11 vs Dapper for bulk inserts, real numbers: at 1M rows EF AddRange takes 21.6 s, Dapper ExecuteAsync 109 s, SqlBulkCopy 7.3 s. Use AddRange under 1,000 rows, SqlBulkCopy (or EFCore.BulkExtensions) above 10,000. Dapper is a full order of magnitude slower than EF for bulk because it has no row batching.

ConfigureAwait(false) in .NET 11: a no-op in ASP.NET Core, console apps, generic-host workers, and async Task xUnit tests, because none of them install a SynchronizationContext. Library code that ships as NuGet or multi-targets netstandard2.0 still needs it on every await, or a caller on WinForms or MAUI will deadlock on .Result.

Azure Functions in-process retires Nov 10, 2026 with .NET 8 LTS. After that date, Azure won't host in-process functions. New apps go isolated worker on .NET 11. The 'in-process is faster on cold start' argument died too: Native AOT isolated now beats in-process p50 (181 ms vs 312 ms on Linux Consumption).

Xamarin.Forms 5.0 to .NET MAUI 11 GA is a one-way trip but mostly mechanical for a medium app: one to three weeks of work. The time sinks are custom renderers becoming handlers with a Mapper dictionary, DependencyService registrations moving to IServiceCollection, and MessagingCenter being retired for CommunityToolkit.Mvvm WeakReferenceMessenger. The win is CoreCLR by default on Android and iOS, generational GC, and cold start under one second on midrange hardware.

Migrating a Blazor Server app to the Blazor Web App template on .NET 11: _Host.cshtml goes, the router moves to Routes.razor, Program.cs swaps MapBlazorHub for MapRazorComponents. Keep pages on InteractiveServer and behaviour is identical. Gotcha: prerendering runs OnInitializedAsync twice; fix with [PersistentState].

ValueTask<T> is a struct that skips the Task<T> heap allocation when an async method completes synchronously, like a cache hit. The price: await it once, never block on .Result, never stash it in a field. A profiler-driven optimization, not a better Task. Turn on CA2012 first, then measure.

A Flutter list that flows into a grid in one scroll: stacking two scrollables with shrinkWrap builds every item on the first frame and gives you fighting scroll positions. The fix is one CustomScrollView of slivers: SliverList, SliverGrid, SliverToBoxAdapter. Plus the childAspectRatio trap that distorts tiles.

EF Core 11 makes named query filters the default way to stack them. Put a soft-delete filter and a tenant filter on the same entity, then call IgnoreQueryFilters(["SoftDeletionFilter"]) to show deleted rows in an admin view without dropping tenant isolation. Plus the required-navigation INNER JOIN trap that silently drops rows.

Switching Claude Code to Manual is one settings line interactively and a silent CI outage headless: every ask becomes a deny and the run still reports success. Worse, an untrusted workspace drops permissions.allow from .claude/settings.json while still applying defaultMode from the same file. Measured on 2.1.224.
